black:
Use case: stylized-concept / reference-guided vehicle artwork.
Asset type: a standalone finished vehicle resource for an existing premium Korean RPG garage collection.
Input image 1 is the requested vehicle DESIGN reference. Input image 2 is an EXISTING GAME VEHICLE used ONLY as the camera, composition, material polish and showroom presentation reference. Do not borrow image 2's car design, badges, body panels or headlights.

COMPOSITION must match image 2: wide 16:9 landscape, low front three-quarter automotive hero view, about 25–35 degrees around from the side, front of the new car at the lower left and rear toward the upper right. Camera slightly above the front wheel center, just enough elevation to read the hood and windshield; not overhead, not isometric, not a straight-on symmetrical frontal view. Long horizontal wheelbase extending across the frame. Front face and the long near side must both be clearly visible. Entire vehicle with all bumper tips, fender blades, tire edges and rear fins fully inside the canvas; about 85 percent of canvas width with generous 6–8 percent side margins, similar visual scale to the existing game vehicle. Show at least the near-side front and rear wheels in coherent perspective, with believable round tires and road contact. It must read as a 4-wheel high-performance CAR, never a jet, hovering vehicle, humanoid robot or tank. A single image of a single vehicle.

BACKDROP and finish: use the same family of high-end dark circular exhibition garage seen in image 2: reflective black stone display floor, restrained circular platform rim, dark architectural walls and broad spaced vertical light strips, gentle overhead light, subtle volumetric depth. Full finished background fills every corner, no transparency or blank studio gradient. The car is the hero, showroom stays unobtrusive. High-end cinematic game vehicle art with convincing clean reflective metal, accurate panel seams, crisp rims and tires, carefully controlled highlights; premium and visually forceful rather than dirty or broken. Enough rim/key lighting to make every dark shape legible. No humans, other vehicles, text, names, item ranks, lettering, watermark, logos, bat emblems or UI. No poster border or inset detail pictures. Do not copy the industrial alley or close-cropped square format of image 1.

VEHICLE DESIGN from image 1: preserve its menacing faceted black/dark gunmetal armored body, deep charcoal and blue-black reflective metal, intricate layered blade-like front fenders, deep V-shaped split front prow and stacked chevron grille, sculpted angular armored hood, narrow ice-white/cool-cyan front lights and inset circular auxiliary lamps. Keep the enclosed dark wraparound cockpit glass integrated into the vehicle, with the distinctive armoured roof shell and swept sculptural rear fins. The helmet-like canopy is architecture on the car, never a literal robotic face or character. Translate the reference's frontal design into the requested low front-three-quarter angle, inventing only the coherent hidden side panels needed for that view. Broad low black wheels sit within the armored fenders; car stays wide, low and planted with a long sports-car wheelbase. The complete front and side armor arrangement should retain the original reference's distinctive sharply faceted and layered character, not become a standard Lamborghini with a bodykit. No oversized unrelated spikes added.
Lighting/effects: silver-white key light and cold cyan reflected accents, nearly-black body stays clearly visible. Very restrained wisps of pale steel-blue energy skimming outside the sill and wheel edges, subtle reflected glow and a few particles, never a thick ring or smoke that obscures the body. Keep the vehicle substantially black and steel, not recolored silver or glowing blue throughout.
